diagnosis_capacity.note: Regularised in-sample effective service budget, not measured staffing or spare capacity.

treatment_capacity.note: Same identification limitation as diagnosis capacity.

queue_split.note: assumed weak prior informed by cancer-specific FDS / 31D label and corroborated cancer types

corroborated_cancer_types.note: Used only to inform a weak split prior; not causal proof.

initial_age_mix.value: Exponential age shapes matched to initial >62-day total and assumed split
initial_age_mix.note: Current age distribution and >104-day count are not observed; final bucket is 365+ days.

diagnosis_min_days.note: Processing eligibility delay; treatment starts no earlier than the day after diagnosis. Referral age is never reset.

service_order.note: Simplified heterogeneous completion order; fractional masses, not individual patient tracking.

capacity_calendar.note: Real rota and service-specific calendars are unavailable.

capacity_variation.note: Monte Carlo service variation; not fitted from staffing data.

strike_factor.note: Editable scenario assumption from the original brief; not a verified trust-level cancer effect.

publication_bridge.value: Simulate from last observation to issue using the latest published flow proxy
publication_bridge.note: The issue-date queue is an unobserved nowcast, not the latest observed backlog.

interpretation.note: Ranges reflect chosen process noise, not calibrated predictive intervals; no personal waits or lives-saved claims.

experiment.note: Editable forcing; simulated strike dates are hypothetical, not a prediction of industrial action.

recovery_tolerance.value: max(5 patients, 5% paired baseline), sustained 14 days after the post-shock excess peak
recovery_tolerance.note: Recovery is censored at the simulation horizon.

recovery.definition: After shock end and the post-shock excess peak, excess over paired baseline <= max(5 patients, 5% baseline) for 14 consecutive days; measured from shock end. If never above tolerance, recovery is zero; non-recovery is censored.
